mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4% over a 3-month window signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 4% for 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 8% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods when UNRATE exceeds 8% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals supply-side weakness, which depresses earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO is below its 12-month MA for four months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) above their respective 6-month moving averages signals a robust demand recovery, which boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both GDPC1 and HOUST exceed their 6-month MAs simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the federal funds rate below 1% combined with a concurrent increase in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 3% signals a policy-lag environment where monetary easing fails to offset inflation, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when FEDFUNDS < 1% and CPIAUCSL > 3%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals a strengthening labor market, which supports consumer spending and corporate profitability, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS is above its 12-month MA for five consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) below its 6-month moving average for three consecutive months, regardless of GDP growth, signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenues and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS is below its 6-month MA for three consecutive months, irrespective of GDP growth.
